How the host is built:
- The class keeps every method, with its docblock, signature and position; each body becomes a literal of exactly the members it reads, plus a `.call`. `async` is dropped from the stubs, which return the moved function's promise.
- Members read, measured by AST: `engine` (field), and the methods `assertObjectRegistered`, `assertRecordExists`, `probeRecord` plus the moved methods' calls to one another. Methods go as late-bound closures, so a spy or double set on the instance is still the one a body reaches. `engine` goes as a getter.
- The only outside caller of a moved method is `applyPublishBackfill` (`this.updateManyData(`), which keeps calling the class method.

Module-level declarations the moved bodies read (all stay in `protocol.ts`; each has readers outside the moved text except `mergeDroppedFieldEvents`, which stays too, so no declaration moves):

Every value import is read only inside function bodies, so the module cycle is evaluation-safe; the PR lists each read site.
- Imports the new module takes from packages directly (as `protocol.ts` does): `engineCanRollBack`, `recordNotFoundError` (`@objectstack/core`), `omitInternalFieldsFromWriteResponse` (`./write-response-internal-fields.js`), and the `@objectstack/spec` types the bodies name.

Path readers migrated in the same PR (each measured base vs head in the PR):
- `scripts/adr-anchors/`: the `protocol.ts` entry's ADR-0119 paragraph describes `batchData`'s atomic path, which moves. Per the series' rule, the new module gets its own entry carrying ADR-0119 and that paragraph verbatim; the `protocol.ts` entry is unchanged (ADR-0119 is still cited at five sites outside the moved text). `check:adr-anchors` decision-letter totals reported base and head.
- `protocol.bracketed-refusal-opener-absence.test.ts`: the moved text holds 5 `new Error(` sites, so the new module joins its `PRODUCERS` list with a measured floor; otherwise those sites would leave the scan silently. `protocol.ts` keeps its floor of 5.
- `docs/adr/0119-…md` anchors `protocol.ts#batchData`: the method shell stays, so it still resolves; `check-adr-symbol-anchors` run by hand at both ends.
- Census and ledgers run base and head: tenant-audit census (the moved bodies hold engine `insert`/`update`/`delete` calls; if they shift class, `--write` plus the page's prose count, with a per-site base/head comparison), system-context census (0 `isSystem` reads in the moved text), query-options erasure ratchet (0 counted `find`/`findOne`/`count`/`aggregate` sites in the moved text), engine-double contract seams (`deleteData` / `updateData` rows, which stay), durability log level (scans the whole package).

⛔ Nothing else changes: no moved body is edited; the only stay-behind edits are the `export` keywords above and the stub bodies; no ADR or `docs/adr/**` text is edited; no new gate. One PR, `skip-changeset` (no behaviour change), `Part of #25467`.

Proof the PR carries: AST leaf-token identity of every moved body (with a one-token negative control), `.d.ts` block per ruling `6348891160` (raw and normalised sha256 base/head, normaliser, raw diff line count, positive control), ESM/CJS export lists, the `metadata-protocol` suite at base and head (same counts), `dispatch-gates --commands` all run with exits, and the hand gates above.
